# Orbit Individual Contributor License Agreement

Draft — have counsel review before relying on it.

This agreement follows the structure of the Apache Software Foundation Individual Contributor License Agreement v2.2, adapted for Orbit.

Thank you for your interest in Orbit (the "Project"), owned by Naram Alhasani (the "Owner"). This agreement records the terms on which you contribute to the Project. It protects you as a contributor and protects the Owner and the Project's users. It does not change your right to use your own Contributions for any other purpose.

You accept this agreement by signing it through the CLA Assistant check on your first pull request. If you contribute on behalf of an employer or other entity, that entity must also agree, or confirm in writing that your Contributions are yours to give.

## 1. Definitions

"You" (or "Your") means the copyright owner, or the person authorized by the copyright owner, that is entering into this agreement with the Owner.

"Contribution" means any original work of authorship, including any modification of or addition to existing work, that You intentionally submit to the Owner for inclusion in the Project. "Submit" means any form of electronic, verbal or written communication sent to the Owner or the Project's representatives, including pull requests, issues, mailing lists and source control, for discussing or improving the Project. It excludes communication You conspicuously mark "Not a Contribution."

You are not expected to provide support for Your Contributions, except to the extent You want to. Unless required by law or agreed in writing, You provide Your Contributions "as is", without warranties or conditions of any kind, express or implied, including warranties or conditions of title, non-infringement, merchantability, or fitness for a particular purpose.

## 7. Work that is not Your own

If You want to submit work that is not Your original creation, submit it separately from any Contribution, identify its source and any license or other restriction You know of (including related patents, trademarks and license agreements), and mark it conspicuously as "Submitted on behalf of a third party: [named here]".
